leads.name: Treurbeuk (Begraafplaats Daalseweg, right of the entrance)

location.address: Right of the entrance gate, Begraafplaats Daalseweg, Nijmegen

leads.why_a_lead: ALREADY PUBLISHED as nij_015 (curation_status flagged, single-source LRMB only) as of this 2026-08-27 pass; not a candidate for new delivery, note kept here only so a future pass does not re-research it from zero looking for a second source. This pass tried again for a second source and still found none: fetched www.gld.nl/lokaal/7550696 (2026 article on sick/dead trees felled at this cemetery) directly and it names conifers and 'oude beuken' generically, felled for giant-fungus infection, but never names or locates the weeping beech at the gate specifically, so it neither confirms nor threatens this tree. Also checked the Gemeente Nijmegen municipal Bomen open-data register (BOR_Groen/GRN_BOMEN, CC-BY, resolved access per data/fetch-blocklist.json 2026-08-26 note) with a tight bbox around this coordinate: zero results, because the cemetery is religious-institution land outside gemeente tree management, confirming the blocklist note's prediction. rijksmonumenten.nl/monument/522938 remains unfetchable (hangs, on the blocklist).

leads.name: Bruine beuk (kerkplein, Petruskerk, Hees)
leads.why_a_lead: Fails only the two-source bar. LRMB register (nr 1680527, status 5, reason monumentaal, n_trees=1, tree-level coordinates, owner_category religieuze instantie, visitable=ja, visible=onbekend) names a single copper beech on the small square at Schependomlaan/Korte Bredestraat in Hees, where Nijmegen's old village church, the Petruskerk, stands (directly fetched: woneninnijmegen.blog/2026/05/02/schependomlaan and nijmeegsglorie.nl/index.php/schependomlaan both confirm the church sits 'aan een pleintje', a small square, at exactly this corner; the tower is on Korte Bredestraat, the church and consistory on Schependomlaan, matching the register's own two-street address). Note the church itself is a former Dutch Reformed (Protestant) building, sold to a private owner in 2020 per the same blog (rented since to Bethel Tempel); this does not by itself disqualify the SQUARE it stands on, which reads as an open village plein rather than an enclosed churchyard, but it is worth flagging since the register's owner_category 'religieuze instantie' may predate that 2020 sale. STATUS ANOMALY, recorded rather than acted on: this entry carries status=5, while its immediate neighbour nr 1680526 (15m away, same square, ALREADY PUBLISHED as nij_016) carries status=3, though both share reason='monumentaal'; checked the register's own status distribution (data/registers/netherlands-lrmb.json) and status 3 and 5 both pair with 'monumentaal' in the large majority of entries nationwide (7,966 and 3,375 respectively), so this looks like a batch or source-provenance code rather than a quality signal, but no schema documentation was found to confirm what the codes mean. No independent source naming THIS beech specifically was found: a monumentaltrees.com page exists for this exact square (title 'Gewone platanen bij de Petruskerk in Nijmegen', URL monumentaltrees.com/nl/nld/gelderland/nijmegen/32428_petruskerk/) but 403'd again on this 2026-08-27 pass, both via WebFetch and via curl -A '<browser UA>' -m 20 (now four failed attempts total across two passes; matches the domain-wide Cloudflare block recorded in data/fetch-blocklist.json, workaround needs a real browser session, not curl/WebFetch). Also tried and hung again this pass: services.nijmegen.nl/geoservices/extern_OpenData/ows (the monumental-tree-specific WFS layer, distinct from the working extern_BOR_Groen bulk-inventory layer); and confirmed the working extern_BOR_Groen municipal layer returns NO trees at all in a tight bbox around this coordinate, because church/religious-institution land sits outside gemeente tree management (same finding as the other two Hees/cemetery leads). Remains unconfirmed by a second source; the sibling plane tree 15m away (nr 1680526) is already published under the same single-source standard, so publishing this one at the same evidence level would be consistent, but that call belongs to whoever merges this file, not to a verification pass that found no new source.

blocked.name: Beuk (Beukenlaan, Landgoed Brakkestein)
blocked.reason: Not a collectible point. Register place field itself reads "Beukenlaan nabij restaurant, Landg. Brakkestein": this stands on one of the beech-lined avenues of Brakkestein's 18th-century sterrenbos (star forest) layout. The Rijksmonument description of Park Brakkenstein (monumenten.nl/monument/522933, fetched directly) states the lanes are largely planted with beech trees ('De lanen zijn grotendeels beplant met beukenbomen'), names a specific beech avenue connecting the two far points of the diamond-shaped grounds, and gives no individual tree special recognition; a separate circle of old beeches exists in the park's northwest corner (a different feature, not this register entry). Independent sources (Digitale Huis 'Sterrenbossen in en om Nijmegen', via WebSearch summary only, page itself 403'd) corroborate that the beeches along the lanes are collectively ~250-300 years old from the original planting, i.e. this register entry is one of a run of similar-aged, similar-looking beeches along a lane rather than a distinguishable individual, the same avenue/whole-wood exclusion BRIEF_RESEARCH.md names explicitly. Planted_band 1700-1750 would make it (if it were a valid standalone entry) the oldest candidate in this batch, so it is recorded here rather than discarded in case a future pass finds it is in fact visually distinct from its neighbours (a girthier trunk, a plaque) that would let it re-qualify.

blocked.name: Mammoetboom Park Leeuwenstein, Nijmegen
blocked.reason: DEAD. This tree fell in the storm of 18 January 2018. Two independent sources, both fetched directly (not summaries): dewester.info/ideeen-gezocht-voor-gesneuvelde-mammoetboom (a 2018 local-news piece titled 'Ideas sought for the fallen mammoth tree', stating 'De storm op 18 januari 2018 joeg ook over de Wolfskuil. In park Leeuwenstein op de grens met het Waterkwartier, ging een hele oude boom, een sequoia, omver', i.e. a very old sequoia in Park Leeuwenstein fell over in that storm, on the Wolfskuil/Waterkwartier border, matching this tree's location); and woneninnijmegen.blog/2023/08/16/park-leeuwenstein (fetched directly, an Aug 2023 post listing the park's trees, stating plainly 'Helaas zijn de 2 grootste bomen afgelopen jaren verloren gegaan: De 24 meter hoge mammoetboom', i.e. the park's 24-metre mammoth tree is one of its 2 largest trees lost in recent years; the same post separately notes a 25.6m swamp cypress/moerascipres also fell in the January 2018 storm, so the park lost two large exotic conifers, not one, and this register entry (n_trees=1, the only mammoetboom the register lists for this park) is the mammoth tree specifically, not the cypress). No source suggests a replacement has been planted at this coordinate. Per hard rule ('we doen niet aan dode bomen') and BRIEF_RESEARCH.md's bar 1, a tree known to be dead is never delivered as a live entry.
